# Implementation Plan: JWT Authentication

**Branch**: `001-ubiquitous-messaging-platform` | **Date**: 2025-11-23 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-ubiquitous-messaging-platform/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by the `/speckit.plan` command for adding JWT authentication to the existing Chat API.

## Summary

Implement simple JWT-based authentication for gRPC endpoints using industry-standard libraries. The feature provides a REST login endpoint that issues JWT tokens, which are then validated by a gRPC interceptor on subsequent requests. This follows a POC-first approach (hardcoded users, plain text passwords) to validate the authentication flow before adding production security layers (MongoDB user storage, BCrypt hashing, refresh tokens).

**Technical Approach** (from research):
- Library: jjwt 0.12.3 (industry standard, Spring Security compatible)
- Algorithm: HS256 symmetric key with static secret (POC simplicity)
- Auth Flow: REST POST /api/auth/login → JWT → gRPC metadata → ServerInterceptor validates
- User Storage: Hardcoded HashMap (POC), MongoDB migration documented
- Password Security: Plain text (POC), BCrypt migration documented

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Java 17 (Spring Boot 3.2.5)
**Primary Dependencies**: 
- jjwt 0.12.3 (JWT generation/validation)
- spring-boot-starter-web 3.2.5 (REST endpoint)
- spring-boot-starter-data-mongodb 3.2.5 (future user storage)
- grpc-spring-boot-starter 2.15.0 (existing, interceptor registration)

**Storage**: 
- POC (Phase 0): In-memory HashMap (3 hardcoded users: alice, bob, admin)
- Production (Phase 1): MongoDB users collection with unique indexes on user_id/username

**Testing**: 
- JUnit 5 (Spring Boot Test)
- Integration tests: Login flow, token validation, expired token, invalid credentials
- Contract tests: POST /api/auth/login endpoint schema
- gRPC tests: Interceptor validation, UNAUTHENTICATED errors

**Target Platform**: 
- Linux/Windows server
- Docker containerized (mongodb, kafka already deployed)
- Ports: 8081 (HTTP auth), 9090 (gRPC), 27017 (MongoDB)

**Project Type**: Backend API (gRPC + REST hybrid)

**Performance Goals**: 
- Login endpoint: <100ms p95 (hash comparison dominates)
- Token validation: <10ms p95 (signature verification)
- No impact on existing gRPC latency (<50ms p95)

**Constraints**: 
- POC must use standard libraries (Constitution Principle VI)
- Plain text passwords acceptable ONLY in POC (documented migration)
- Secret key must be configurable (application.properties, later env var)
- Zero breaking changes to existing endpoints

**Scale/Scope**: 
- POC: 3 users (alice, bob, admin)
- Production Phase 1: 10k users (MongoDB indexed)
- Token expiration: 24 hours (configurable)
- Concurrent logins: No session limit (stateless JWT)

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### Pre-Design Validation ✅ PASSED

**Principle I (Educational Code Quality)**: 
- ✅ JWT authentication is a fundamental distributed systems concept (security at API boundaries)
- ✅ Code will demonstrate clear patterns (JwtService, Interceptor) with step-by-step validation logic
- ✅ Every design decision documented with "why" rationale (see research.md)

**Principle II (Explicit Responsibility)**:
- ✅ All components have single responsibility documented in data-model.md
  - JwtService: Token generation/validation ONLY
  - AuthenticationController: Login endpoint ONLY (no business logic)
  - JwtAuthenticationInterceptor: Token validation ONLY (no authorization logic)
- ✅ Clear boundaries: "Does NOT handle password hashing" (UserService responsibility)

**Principle III (Descriptive Naming)**:
- ✅ All entity names follow standards: `LoginRequest`, `UserInfo`, `JwtAuthenticationInterceptor`
- ✅ No abbreviations: `maximumTokenExpirationMilliseconds` (not `maxExpMs`)
- ✅ Boolean fields: `isTokenExpired()`, `hasValidSignature()`

**Principle IV (Test-Driven Development)**:
- ✅ POC acceptance criteria defines tests FIRST (see research.md)
- ✅ Integration test specified: login → token → gRPC call → validate user context
- ✅ Contract test required: POST /api/auth/login endpoint schema

**Principle V (Performance with Scalability)**:
- ✅ JWT validation is stateless (no session storage, enables horizontal scaling)
- ✅ Token expiration prevents indefinite token validity
- ✅ Performance target documented: <10ms token validation p95

**Principle VI (Clear Architecture & Transparency)**:
- ✅ Technology choice justified: jjwt library (standard, not custom JWT implementation)
- ✅ Algorithm choice documented: HS256 (POC simplicity vs RS256 key management complexity)
- ✅ No "magic" annotations: Interceptor registration explicit in configuration

**Principle VII (Documentation-First)**:
- ✅ Full design documented BEFORE implementation (research.md, data-model.md, quickstart.md)
- ✅ API contracts specified (POST /api/auth/login request/response schemas)
- ✅ Migration path to production documented (BCrypt, MongoDB, refresh tokens)

**Principle VIII (Incremental Delivery & Pragmatic Scope)**:
- ✅ **POC-First Approach**: Hardcoded HashMap users validate JWT flow WITHOUT MongoDB complexity
- ✅ **Standard Library Reuse**: jjwt library (not custom token implementation)
- ✅ **Layer-by-Layer**: POC (hardcoded users) → P1 (MongoDB) → P2 (BCrypt) → P3 (refresh tokens)
- ✅ **Educational Transparency**: Plain text passwords documented as POC-only with migration plan

### Post-Design Validation (After Phase 1)

**Re-check after contracts/ generation**:
- [ ] REST endpoint schema validated with OpenAPI spec
- [ ] gRPC metadata format documented in contracts/README.md
- [ ] Error responses follow gRPC status code semantics (UNAUTHENTICATED, PERMISSION_DENIED)

**Complexity Introduced**: None (POC uses standard patterns)
- No custom serialization (JWT standard format)
- No reflection beyond Spring Boot defaults
- No database schema changes in POC (MongoDB deferred to P1)

**GATE DECISION**: ✅ **APPROVED TO PROCEED** - All principles satisfied. POC scope clearly defined with production migration path.

**Structure Decision**: 

This feature adds JWT authentication to the existing Chat API codebase following hexagonal architecture patterns already established. Key design choices:

1. **Separation of Concerns**: 
   - `JwtService`: Pure token logic (generate, validate, extract claims) - no HTTP/gRPC knowledge
   - `AuthenticationController`: HTTP boundary adapter - delegates to JwtService
   - `JwtAuthenticationInterceptor`: gRPC boundary adapter - delegates to JwtService
   - `UserService`: User lookup abstraction - enables HashMap → MongoDB migration without changing other components

2. **Configuration Isolation**:
   - `JwtConfig` centralizes secret/expiration loading from application.properties
   - Enables environment variable override in production: `${JWT_SECRET:fallback-secret}`

3. **Test Organization**:
   - Unit tests per service (fast feedback, no infrastructure)
   - Integration test validates full flow (REST login → gRPC call with token)
   - Contract test ensures API schemas match documentation

4. **POC Simplicity**:
   - No repository layer in POC (UserService uses HashMap directly)
   - No BCrypt dependency yet (plain text comparison in UserService)
   - No refresh token logic (single-token flow)
   - Migration path: Swap UserService implementation to UserRepository in Phase 1 without touching JwtService/controllers/interceptor

## Complexity Tracking

> **No Complexity Justification Required**

This feature introduces JWT authentication using industry-standard patterns and libraries, fully compliant with Constitution Principle VIII (Incremental Delivery & Pragmatic Scope).

### POC-First Validation ✅

**POC Scope** (Phase 0 - Current):
- Hardcoded HashMap users (alice, bob, admin) - validates authentication flow
- Plain text password comparison - enables debugging without BCrypt overhead
- Static JWT secret in application.properties - simplifies configuration
- Single token type (access token only) - no refresh token complexity

**Production Migration Path** (Phases 1-3):
- **Phase 1**: Replace HashMap with MongoDB UserRepository, add BCrypt password hashing
- **Phase 2**: Move JWT secret to environment variable, add refresh token support
- **Phase 3**: Add rate limiting, token blacklist, monitoring

**Educational Rationale**:
POC demonstrates JWT fundamentals (signature validation, claims extraction, expiration) without infrastructure complexity. Students validate the authentication flow works BEFORE adding MongoDB users, BCrypt hashing, and refresh token rotation.

### Standard Library Usage ✅

**Library**: jjwt 0.12.3 (io.jsonwebtoken)
**Justification**: Industry-standard JWT library, Spring Security compatible, no custom token logic required

**Alternative Rejected**: Custom JWT implementation  
**Reason**: Violates Principle VIII (Standard Library Reuse). Implementing HMAC signature generation, Base64URL encoding, and claim validation from scratch would:
- Introduce security vulnerabilities (timing attacks, weak random number generation)
- Require extensive cryptography testing
- Distract from distributed systems learning goals (authentication flow patterns, not crypto primitives)

### Architecture Simplicity ✅

**No New Patterns Introduced**:
- Interceptor pattern already used in existing gRPC stack (not new)
- REST controller pattern already established (AuthenticationController follows existing pattern)
- Service layer separation already standard in codebase (JwtService, UserService match existing design)

**No Breaking Changes**:
- Existing endpoints remain publicly accessible during POC (whitelisted in interceptor)
- Gradual enforcement: Can add `@RequiresAuthentication` annotation per-endpoint later
- Backward compatible: Clients without tokens get clear UNAUTHENTICATED error
